correctness.rationale: For n≥4 and 2≤k≤n−2, the first real Johnson harmonic is f_a(S)=∑_{i∈S}a_i with ∑a_i=0, probability-uniform k-subset S. Inclusion-indicator factorial moments give E f²=c s₂ and E f⁴=A s₂²+B s₄ with c=k(n-k)/(n(n−1)), B=k(n-k)[n(n+1)−6k(n−k)]/[n(n−1)(n−2)(n−3)]. The real zero-sum unit sphere is compact and smooth. A Lagrange cubic gives at most three coordinate values. Sign-definite constrained Hessian directions rule out three-valued global minima and yield a strictly suboptimal 1/2 value for the only three-valued candidate maximum. Two-value vectors then give T+= (n²−3n+3)/(n(n−1)) and T-=n/(floor(n/2)ceil(n/2))−3/n. The sign of B selects one-spike versus balanced equality, with all nonzero directions equal at B=0, e.g. (8,2). Independent exact subset enumeration on (4,2),(8,2),(10,3),(14,6) confirmed the formulas and branch values. Finite enumerations are corroborative of the global Hessian proof.
